sources.entry: Manticore Search - Full-text search and data analytics, with fast response time for small, medium and big data (alternative to Elasticsearch). GPL-3.0 Docker/deb/C++/K8S

summary.one_liner: Manticore Search is an open-source, C++-based database and search engine for full-text search and data analytics, positioned as an alternative to Elasticsearch.
summary.what_it_does: Manticore Search provides full-text search with inverted indexes, ranking and custom ranking, plus filtering, fuzzy, faceted, geo-spatial, and vector/hybrid search. It supports row-wise, columnar, and docstore storage, letting users trade RAM use against speed. Data can be queried with SQL over MySQL-compatible clients, an HTTP JSON API, and Elasticsearch-compatible writes. It can sync data from MySQL, PostgreSQL, ODBC, MS SQL, Kafka, XML, and CSV. The README also describes replication (Galera-based), sharded tables, authentication, and backup tools including SQL BACKUP and manticore-backup.
use_cases: full-text search for a website or application
log and event analytics on large datasets
vector and hybrid search over text
syncing MySQL or PostgreSQL data into a fast search index
how_to_run: curl | sh  (one-line installer for Linux and macOS with Homebrew; URL not shown in README)
sudo apt install ./manticore-repo.noarch.deb && sudo apt update && sudo apt install manticore  (Debian/Ubuntu)
notable: Speaks SQL and MySQL protocol, with an HTTP JSON API and Elasticsearch-compatible writes
Row-wise, columnar, and docstore storage options for RAM vs. speed trade-offs
Hybrid full-text plus vector search, auto-embeddings with automatic chunking, and conversational search via SQL CALL CHAT
Built-in sharding, Galera-based multi-master replication, and load balancing
Around 40MB RSS for an empty instance, per the README
caveats: Not fully ACID-compliant, according to the README
Columnar storage gives lower performance than row-wise for some query types
Docstore cannot sort, group, or filter, only fetch original values
Native Windows support is described only through separate instructions; WSL is the documented path
